statement: A bus leaves every 15 minutes starting at 7:00 am. What time does the sixth bus leave?

choices.misconception: I added 75 minutes to the hour without converting past sixty.
I counted six gaps of fifteen minutes rather than five.
I added ninety minutes but wrote it as a time without converting.
I counted six gaps and then added one more.

hints: The first bus leaves after no waiting at all.
Count the gaps rather than the buses: reaching the sixth bus takes five gaps of fifteen minutes. Work out the total minutes, then convert into hours before adding to the start time.
Five gaps of 15 minutes is 75 minutes after 7:00.

solutions.reliable: The sixth bus is five gaps after the first, so 5 x 15 = 75 minutes after 7:00, which is 8:15. The transferable idea: count the gaps, not the items, because the first item takes no gaps to reach, and convert minutes into hours before writing a time.

whyOnTest: Counting buses instead of gaps, and writing more than sixty minutes into a time, are both offered as choices.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
